Like many older downtown commercial buildings that have been repurposed and re-leased over the decades, the Insurance Exchange Building houses general office tenants rather than a data center business. The telecom=data_center tag most likely reflects a telecommunications or IT equipment room within the building, used to serve its office tenants' internet and phone connectivity, rather than an actual wholesale or retail colocation operation open to outside data-center customers. This entry documents that likely mistag honestly, in keeping with the project's policy of noting a short, accurate correction rather than fabricating data-center specifications, such as IT capacity or technical square footage, for a building that functions as conventional office space.

The Insurance Exchange Building is a facility in downtown Denver at 910 15th Street with no published power specification and no identified operator. It appears in OpenStreetMap as a named building but without any available operator website, contact information, or technical detail. Research to identify the operator has been exhausted with no result.

Colorado has seventeen mapped data center facilities of which only three publish power figures, totaling 26.35 MW. This building, lacking any published specification, cannot be ranked among them by capacity and plays no measurable role in the state's stated AI infrastructure.

Without power specifications, address confirmation beyond a building name, or operator identity, this facility cannot be assessed for relevance to AI compute scaling. Future research with access to building databases or operator registries may establish whether it hosts compute infrastructure at scale, or serves another purpose entirely.
